land.text: East Java: 'Airlangga ... re-established the kingdom ... under the name of kingdom of Kahuripan in 1019'

successors.note: The page names Kahuripan as the successor state; Cliopatria has nothing for Java in 1010-1027 apart from Galuh and Sunda.

capitals.name: Mataram (Central Java)
capitals.note: Infobox capitals: Mataram (Central Java), Mamrati (Pikatan, 838-850), Poh Pitu (Balitung, Daksha, Tulodong); the Sanjaya page has the first centre at Ukir Hill and the kraton moving in 742-755. Coordinates are the Yogyakarta-Prambanan core, not a located palace.

capitals.name: Tamwlang and Watugaluh (East Java)
capitals.note: 'Around the year 929, the centre of the kingdom was shifted from Central Java to East Java by Mpu Sindok'; Watugaluh was destroyed in the attack on Dharmawangsa (Airlangga page). Site approximate (Brantas valley).

capitals.name: Wwatan (East Java)
capitals.note: Dharmawangsa's capital; the page dates his reign only as 'c. 990s'. Site approximate (Madiun country).

rulers.name: Sanjaya
rulers.note: '716/717-746 or 732 onward; sources vary' (Sanjaya page: 716-746 or 732-760).

rulers.name: Pikatan
rulers.note: Married the Shailendra princess Pramodhawardhani; defeated Balaputra in 852.

rulers.name: Balitung
rulers.note: 'came to the throne on 10 May 898 and ruled for approximately 12 years'.

rulers.name: Wawa
rulers.note: The page gives no end year for Sindok (c. 929, founder of the Isyana dynasty) or the later kings, so the list stops here.

correction.text: Central Java, Sanjaya's core from c. 717 (the page: 'Central Java was the core')

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria starts Mataram in 741, but the page says 'It seemed that Sanjaya came to power c. 717 AD' (the Sanjaya page: 716, from Damais's Saka 638) and the Canggal inscription is dated 732. Central Java was the core; the page gives no extent for Sanjaya's first years.

union.text: Central Java: 'Central Java was the core', the Yogyakarta-Prambanan-Klaten country and Kedu (the part of Jawa Tengah and Yogyakarta inside Cliopatria's Mataram shape, which leaves out the western districts that are Galuh's)

correction.text: Central Java plus Galuh, 'came under Mataram influence'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Sanjaya's invasion of Galuh in 723 (Purbasora 'killed in 723'; Premanadikusuma 'appointed by Sanjaya', 723-732; his son Tamperan 732-739) puts the Galuh country inside Mataram's reach until Manarah's revolt of 739. Cliopatria draws these years inside its Sunda Kingdom row (62,498 and 121,225 km2).

correction.text: Central Java only, 741-897; the East Java land comes with Balitung from 898

keyframe_review.note: 59,610 km2 for 741-1002 (109.2-113.1E) reaches East Java to the Surabaya coast. The page has Central Java as the core and Balitung (from 898) 'brought parts of East Java into the kingdom', influence running from Cilacap through Kedu and Prambanan 'and the Brantas valley to the Malang highlands'. So the 741 shape is Central Java only to 897; Cliopatria's shape is restored from 898 in the next keyframe. No infobox area.

correction.text: Central Java and the Brantas valley to the Malang highlands: Cliopatria's 741 shape held from 898

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 898-1002: Cliopatria's 741 shape (59,610 km2, Central and East Java) held from Balitung's accession on 10 May 898; East Java stays Mataram's after Sindok's move there c. 929.

59,610 km2 for 1003-1009: the same shape, re-dated by Cliopatria at 1003. The Airlangga page dates the Wurawari destruction of Mataram to 1006 and the Mataram page to 1016-1017; Cliopatria stops in 1009.

correction.text: unchanged shape held from 1010 to 1016, the year of the Wurawari revolt

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 1010-1016: the infobox gives '732 AD-1016' and the Pucangan inscription has 'Haji (king) Wurawari to revolt' in 1016-1017, so the shape runs seven years past Cliopatria's last year. The shape is the 1003 shape unchanged.

region.text: Central Java: 'Central Java was the core', the Yogyakarta-Prambanan-Klaten country and Kedu (the part of Jawa Tengah and Yogyakarta inside Cliopatria's Mataram shape, which leaves out the western districts that are Galuh's)

ledger.note: c. 717: Sanjaya comes to power in Central Java. 'It seemed that Sanjaya came to power c. 717 AD'; the earliest account of the kingdom is the Canggal inscription of 732, and the Sanjaya page gives 716 (Damais) and the reign as 716-746 or 732-760.

region.text: Galuh, the country east of the Citarum

ledger.note: 723: Sanjaya takes Galuh. Purbasora 'killed in 723' in the invasion; Premanadikusuma 'appointed by Sanjaya' ruled 723-732 and Galuh 'came under Mataram influence'. The page does not describe the campaign.

region.text: Galuh, the country east of the Citarum

ledger.note: 739: Galuh is lost. Tamperan Barmawijaya (732-739), Sanjaya's son, was 'killed by Manarah in 739', who reigned 739-783. Cliopatria's Galuh row resumes in 741.

minus.text: Central Java: 'Central Java was the core', the Yogyakarta-Prambanan-Klaten country and Kedu (the part of Jawa Tengah and Yogyakarta inside Cliopatria's Mataram shape, which leaves out the western districts that are Galuh's)

region.text: East Java: the Brantas valley and the Malang highlands, in Cliopatria's 741 shape but not in Central Java

ledger.note: 898: East Java joins (the year is Balitung's accession, 10 May 898; the page dates no conquest). 'Balitung brought parts of East Java into the kingdom', his influence reaching 'the Brantas valley to the Malang highlands'.
c. 929: the court goes to East Java. 'Around the year 929, the centre of the kingdom was shifted from Central Java to East Java by Mpu Sindok'; Tamwlang and Watugaluh become the seats.
c. 929: Mpu Sindok founds the Isyana dynasty in East Java. The page names him 'founder of the Isyana dynasty'; the kingdom, its colour and the East Java land continue (rule 2).

region.text: Bali, 'probably a vassal' through Mahendradatta's marriage to Udayana

ledger.note: c. 990: Bali becomes Mataram's vassal, probably. Bali 'probably was an ally or vassal of Java' in the 11th century; the marriage of Mahendradatta, Dharmawangsa's sister, to Udayana was 'probably ... a political means to seal Bali as part of Mataram's realm'. The page dates neither; the Mataram page has Bali 'probably' a vassal in Dharmawangsa's time ('c. 990s').

region.text: Bali, 'probably a vassal' through Mahendradatta's marriage to Udayana

ledger.note: 1016: Mataram falls and Bali is on its own (page silent: nothing says what became of Bali's tie).

region.text: Mataram's last shape, East Java with Central Java

ledger.note: 1016: the Wurawari revolt destroys Mataram. Infobox '732 AD-1016'; 'Pucangan inscription describe in 1016-1017, Haji (king) Wurawari to revolt'; Airlangga 'established the kingdom of Kahuripan in 1019'. The Airlangga page gives 1006 for the same destruction of Dharmawangsa's capital.

wars.name: Sanjaya's invasion of Galuh

zones.text: Galuh, the country east of the Citarum

wars.outcome: Purbasora killed in 723; Premanadikusuma installed; Galuh under Mataram influence until Manarah's revolt of 739.

wars.name: Mataram-Srivijayan wars
wars.outcome: No land changes hands: the Anjukladang inscription of 937 'mentions an infiltration attack from Malayu'; 'In 990, King Dharmawangsa of Java launched a naval invasion against Srivijaya'; in 1006 Srivijaya repelled the Javanese invasion; the infobox gives 'c. 937-1016'.

wars.name: Wurawari revolt against Dharmawangsa
wars.outcome: Dharmawangsa killed and the capital destroyed (the 'Pralaya of Mataram'); Airlangga escapes and founds Kahuripan in 1019.
wars.note: The Airlangga page dates it 1006 and says historians suggest Srivijaya incited it; the Mataram page's inscription dates are 1016-1017. Closed at 1016, the end of the state's life; the inscription's span is 1016-1017.

certainty.note: The inscriptions give centres and rulers, never frontiers; the East Java reach is from the Balitung description only.

notes: Start 717 (Sanjaya's accession, 'c. 717') against the infobox's 732 (the Canggal inscription), so that the 723 conquest of Galuh falls inside the state's life; Cliopatria starts 741. End 1016 (infobox) against Cliopatria's 1009 and the Airlangga page's 1006; 1010-1027 has no Cliopatria shape for Java except Galuh and Sunda. Cliopatria's single 741 shape (59,610 km2, to the Surabaya coast) is cut to Central Java until Balitung's 898 on the strength of the page's 'Central Java was the core ... Balitung brought parts of East Java': a reading, no page dates the East Java conquest. Cliopatria draws 724-740 inside its Sunda row; the Galuh and Sunda dossiers correct that. The Sailendra dynasty, which patronised Borobudur (825) and whom Pikatan's Sanjaya line defeated in 852 (Balaputra), is not covered by any Cliopatria row and was not opened: counterpart without a dossier (Central Java, c. 775-852). Bali as a Mataram vassal c. 990-1016 is 'probably' on the page and recorded at confidence 1. Capital coordinates are approximate. Wurawari (the 1016 rebel) needs no dossier. No infobox area. Page budget 1-2: five pages cited, three shared with other dossiers.
